questions.solution:

y's share = Rs. 2,400

Total amount = (Sum of ratios) × Individual share

y's ratio part = 3

⇒ 1 part = Rs. 2,400 / 3 = Rs. 800

Total parts = 4 + 3 = 7

**⇒ Total initial amount = 7 parts = 7 × Rs. 800 = Rs. 5,600**

questions.question: Electric power consumed by two electric bulbs (each with 5 Ω resistance) connected in series with a 3 V battery is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.9 W**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Two 5 Ω bulbs in **series** give total resistance: Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 5+5 = 10 Ω.
 
• Current from a 3 V source: I = V/R = 3/10 = 0.3 A (Ohm’s law V = IR).
 
• Total power drawn: P = V²/R = 3²/10 = 0.9 W (equivalently P = VI). 
 
• Each bulb dissipates Pbᵤₗb = I²R = (0.3)² × 5 = 0.45 W; sum of bulb powers equals 0.9 W.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Series vs. Parallel:** In series, the same current flows through all elements; in parallel, the same voltage appears across each branch.
 
• **Equivalent Resistance:** Series resistances add (Rₛ = ΣR); in parallel, 1/Rₚ = Σ(1/R). 
 
• **Power Identities:** P = VI = I²R = V²/R (from combining power with Ohm’s law).
 
• **What if parallel?** Two 5 Ω bulbs in parallel → R = 2.5 Ω; P = V²/R = 9/2.5 = 3.6 W (greater than series). 
 
• **SI Units:** ampere (A) for current, ohm (Ω) for resistance, watt (W) for power (SI-defined).

questions.question: As per a news report in March 2022, scientists at the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS) designed an electrocatalyst system for energy-efficient production of ________ with the help of electrolysis of urea.
questions.solution:

questions.question: An incident ray passes through the focus of a concave mirror. The reflected ray:

options.text: is parallel to the principal axis
passes through the centre of curvature
passes through the focus of the mirror

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**is parallel to the principal axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An incident ray that passes through the focus of a concave mirror will reflect parallel to the principal axis.
 
• This is due to the property of concave mirrors where rays passing through the focus reflect parallel to the principal axis.
 
• The principal axis is the line that passes through the center of curvature and the focus, extending to infinity on both sides.
 
• This property is used in various optical devices to direct light in a specific direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror with a reflecting surface that curves inward.
 
• It is also known as a converging mirror because it converges light to a point.
 
 
 
• **Principal Axis:**
 
 
• The principal axis is a straight line that passes through the pole (the midpoint of the mirror) and the center of curvature of the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Focus (Focal Point):**
 
 
• The focus of a concave mirror is the point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to converge after reflecting off the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Center of Curvature:**
 
 
• The center of curvature is the center of the sphere of which the concave mirror is a part.

questions.question: The larger of two supplementary angles is 36° more than the smaller. The smaller angle is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Larger angle = Smaller angle + 36°, Supplementary angles sum = 180°

**Formula:**

Larger angle + Smaller angle = 180°

**Calculation:**

Let's denote Smaller angle = S, Larger angle = L

L = S + 36°

⇒ S + (S + 36°) = 180°

⇒ 2S + 36° = 180°

⇒ 2S = 180° - 36°

⇒ 2S = 144°

⇒ S = 144° / 2

⇒ S = 72°

**Smaller angle = 72°**

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added a new part IV-A to the Indian Constitution, which enshrines the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• Article 51A, specifically, lists ten Fundamental Duties for every citizen of India.
 
• These duties include respecting the Constitution, the national flag, and the national anthem; cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle; and upholding and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• Other duties involve promoting harmony, safeguarding public property, protecting the environment, and striving towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.

• The 42nd Amendment, enacted in 1976, is one of the most significant amendments as it brought about extensive changes, including the addition of the Fundamental Duties.
 
 
 
• **Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Part IV-A was added to the Constitution through the 42nd Amendment and it deals with Fundamental Duties. This part aims to remind citizens that while they enjoy their rights, they also have certain duties to perform.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR. They are non-justiciable, which means they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties was intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens that they should be conscious of their duties towards their country, society, and fellow citizens.
 
• These duties help in promoting a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens, which is essential for the unity and integrity of the nation.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 20 and their difference is 16. The ratio of the larger number to the smaller number is:
questions.solution:

A + B = 20 

A - B = 16 

**Calculation:**

A + B = 20 (Equation 1)

A - B = 16 (Equation 2)

(A + B) + (A - B) = 20 + 16 2A = 36 A = 36 / 2 A = 18

18 + B = 20 B = 20 - 18 B = 2

**Therefore, the ratio of the larger number to the smaller number (A : B) is 18 : 2, which can be simplified to 9:1.**

questions.question: Out of indigo, green, orange and yellow colours, which colour has the least refractive index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Orange**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Orange light has a lower refractive index compared to indigo, green, and yellow lights.
 
• The refractive index of a color decreases as the wavelength of the light increases. Orange light has a longer wavelength compared to indigo, green, and yellow.
 
• Refractive index is inversely related to the speed of light in the medium. Orange light, having a lower refractive index, travels faster in a medium compared to indigo, green, and yellow lights.
 
• Therefore, among the given options, orange light bends the least when passing through a prism, indicating it has the lowest refractive index.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Refractive Index:**

 
 
• The refractive index of a material is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced inside the material compared to the speed of light in a vacuum.
 
• It is a dimensionless number, typically greater than 1, and is denoted by the letter 'n'.
 
• The refractive index can be calculated using the formula n = c/v, where c is the speed of light in a vacuum and v is the speed of light in the material.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion of Light:**
 
 
• When light passes through a prism, it is separated into its constituent colors, a process known as dispersion.
 
• Different colors of light bend by different amounts due to their varying refractive indices.
 
• Violet and indigo light, having shorter wavelengths, bend more than red and orange light, which have longer wavelengths.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength and Frequency:**
 
 
• The wavelength of light is the distance between successive peaks of the electromagnetic waves.
 
• Frequency is the number of wave cycles that pass a point per unit time, typically measured in hertz (Hz).
 
• There is an inverse relationship between wavelength and frequency: λ = c/f, where λ is the wavelength, c is the speed of light, and f is the frequency.
 
 
 
• **Prisms and Light Bending:**
 
 
• A prism is a transparent optical element with flat, polished surfaces that refract light.
 
• The angle at which light enters and exits the prism affects how much it bends and how it is dispersed into its constituent colors.
 
• Prisms are commonly used in spectrometers to analyze light and determine the wavelengths present in a light source.
 
 

The correct answer is **Option 2**__.

• **Endothermic Reaction**

• Sigma tropic reactions are a class of pericyclic reactions where a sigma bond adjacent to one or more pi systems shifts to a new position in the molecule, resulting in a new sigma bond.

questions.question: What role does transpiration play in the transport of water in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It exerts a suction force.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Transpiration** is the process by which water vapor is lost from the aerial parts of the plant, primarily through the stomata of leaves.
 
• This process creates a negative pressure (suction force) in the leaf's air spaces, which pulls water from the roots up through the xylem vessels.
 
• **Water molecules** stick together due to cohesion and stick to the walls of xylem vessels due to adhesion, aiding in water transport.
 
• Transpiration helps in the upward movement of water and dissolved nutrients from the roots to the leaves, known as the transpiration pull.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem**

 
 
• Xylem is one of the two types of transport tissue in vascular plants, the other being phloem.
 
• The primary function of xylem is to transport water and nutrients from the roots to the shoots and leaves.
 
• Xylem tissue consists of tracheids, vessel elements, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibers.
 
 
 
• **Stomata**
 
 
• Stomata are tiny openings or pores in plant tissue that allow for gas exchange.
 
• They are found primarily on the surface of leaves.
 
• Stomata play a critical role in the process of transpiration and photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Cohesion-Tension Theory**
 
 
• This theory explains the mechanism of water movement from roots to leaves in plants.
 
• According to this theory, water is pulled up the xylem vessels by the cohesive forces between water molecules and the tension created by transpiration.
 
• This continuous column of water is maintained due to the cohesive properties of water molecules.
 
 
 
• **Adhesion**
 
 
• Adhesion refers to the attraction between water molecules and the walls of xylem vessels.
 
• This property helps in the upward movement of water against gravity.

• Carbonic acid is also present in carbonated beverages, giving them their fizz.

questions.question: The correct relation between P, V, R and I amongst the following is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P = I²R**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ohm's Law** states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula P = I²R comes from the combination of Ohm's Law (V = IR) and the formula for power (P = VI).
 
• By substituting V from Ohm's Law (V = IR) into the power formula (P = VI), we get P = I²R.
 
• This formula is used to calculate the power dissipated in a resistor when the current flowing through it is known.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Power (P):**

 
 
• Power is the rate at which electrical energy is transferred by an electric circuit. The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
 
• In electrical circuits, power can be calculated using the formula P = VI, where V is the voltage and I is the current.
 
 
 
• **Voltage (V):**
 
 
• Voltage is the electrical potential difference between two points in a circuit. It is the force that pushes electric charges to flow through a conductor. The SI unit of voltage is the volt (V).
 
 
 
• **Current (I):**
 
 
• Current is the flow of electric charge in a conductor. It is measured in amperes (A).
 
• According to Ohm's Law, current (I) can be calculated using the formula I = V/R, where V is the voltage and R is the resistance.
 
 
 
• **Resistance (R):**
 
 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of current in a conductor. It is measured in ohms (Ω).
 
• Resistance can be calculated using the formula R = V/I, where V is the voltage and I is the current.

questions.question: Which of the following animals is present on the insignia of Reserve Bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tiger**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The insignia of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) features a strong and majestic tiger.
 
• This symbol was chosen to reflect the strength and resilience of the Indian economy.
 
• The tiger in the RBI logo is depicted standing under a palm tree.
 
• The insignia signifies the RBI's commitment to the economic welfare of the country and its role as a central banking institution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is India's central banking institution, which controls the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• It commenced its operations on 1 April 1935 in accordance with the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India.
 
• It is responsible for regulating the country's currency and credit systems to ensure monetary stability and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Central Bank**
 
 
• A central bank is an institution that manages a state's currency, money supply, and interest rates.
 
• Central banks also oversee the commercial banking system of their respective countries.
 
• Examples include the Federal Reserve in the United States, the European Central Bank (ECB), and the Bank of England (BoE).
 
• Central banks conduct monetary policy to achieve goals like controlling inflation, managing employment levels, and maintaining financial stability.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy**
 
 
• Monetary policy refers to the actions undertaken by a central bank to control the money supply and achieve macroeconomic goals such as inflation control, consumption, growth, and liquidity.
 
• It involves the management of interest rates and the total supply of money in circulation.
 
• Tools of monetary policy include open market operations, reserve requirements, and interest rate changes.
 
• Effective monetary policy helps stabilize the economy and promotes sustainable growth.

questions.question: Who is believed to be the first person to bring Christianity to India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saint Thomas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Saint Thomas, also known as Doubting Thomas, is believed to be one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ who brought Christianity to India.
 
• According to tradition, he arrived in India in AD 52 and preached the gospel, establishing several churches.
 
• His missionary work is particularly associated with the region of Kerala, on the southwestern coast of India.
 
• Saint Thomas is said to have been martyred near Chennai (formerly Madras) and is commemorated in various Christian traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Christianity in India**

 
 
• Christianity is India's third-largest religion, with about 2.3% of the population identifying as Christians.
 
• The faith has a long history in India, with traditions dating back to the arrival of Saint Thomas.
 
• Various Christian denominations exist in India, including Roman Catholic, Protestant, and Orthodox churches.
 
• Kerala, Goa, and northeastern states have significant Christian populations, with many communities tracing their heritage back to early missionaries.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• Saint Thomas's arrival in India coincided with the early spread of Christianity in the first century AD.
 
• This period saw the establishment of Christian communities in the Roman Empire and beyond.
 
• Saint Thomas's mission in India is part of the larger history of the apostolic age, when the apostles spread the teachings of Jesus worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Saint Thomas's Legacy**
 
 
• Saint Thomas is venerated as a saint in various Christian traditions, including the Roman Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, and Anglican churches.
 
• His feast day is celebrated on July 3rd, known as Saint Thomas Day.
 
• Several churches and places of pilgrimage in India are dedicated to his memory, reflecting his lasting influence on Indian Christianity.
